cases.name: Explicit source version, stable route and no clinical approval
Significant historical VTE remains NCCP exclusion

findings.text: A history of significant thromboembolic disease is an NCCP exclusion. Do not administer without specialist reconciliation; the breast-cancer SmPC uses individual risk–benefit wording and does not override this NCCP restriction.
Withhold tamoxifen for active or recent VTE and arrange oncology review. An acute event requires immediate treatment; any restart is a specialist risk–benefit decision, not automatic clearance.
Withhold tamoxifen and arrange urgent assessment of suspected DVT / pulmonary embolism. Do not wait for a routine clinic.

Arrange prompt gynaecological evaluation of abnormal bleeding, discharge or pelvic symptoms. NCCP specifies investigation; it does not mandate an automatic dose reduction or blanket treatment interruption.
Arrange ophthalmic assessment for new visual disturbance; continuation is an individual clinical decision.
Avoid potent CYP2D6 inhibitors where possible because they lower active endoxifen exposure. Oncology/pharmacy should agree alternatives; do not abruptly stop a prescribed antidepressant.

Tamoxifen can enhance coumarin anticoagulation: reconcile medicines and arrange close INR monitoring. The primary-prevention contraindication must not be imported as an automatic breast-cancer-treatment contraindication.
CYP3A4 induction may lower tamoxifen exposure; ask oncology pharmacy to review the combination. No empirical dose increase is specified.

Agree thrombosis prevention and any temporary interruption with oncology and the surgical team. For breast-cancer treatment there is no universal six-week stop rule; that wording concerns other indications.

cases.name: Coumarin treatment is not a cancer-treatment contraindication

findings.text: Tamoxifen can enhance coumarin anticoagulation: reconcile medicines and arrange close INR monitoring. The primary-prevention contraindication must not be imported as an automatic breast-cancer-treatment contraindication.

Agree thrombosis prevention and any temporary interruption with oncology and the surgical team. For breast-cancer treatment there is no universal six-week stop rule; that wording concerns other indications.

Concurrent tamoxifen and anastrozole requires prescriber/pharmacy reconciliation: the Irish Tamox SmPC reports no added efficacy from an adjuvant aromatase-inhibitor combination, while some UK product labels contraindicate concurrent anastrozole. Confirm the prescribed sequence and dispensed product; do not treat sequential switching as concurrent use. No automatic dose is assigned.

cases.name: Risk-triggered ECG does not create universal four-week test

findings.text: Review cardiac/QT risk and interacting medicines. NCCP and the Irish Tamox SmPC support ECG and electrolyte monitoring when risk makes it indicated; agree follow-up from the actual product information and clinical findings. Do not apply a universal fixed-cycle ECG or echocardiogram schedule.

New palpitations, dizziness or syncope need prompt clinical assessment, ECG and electrolyte review; syncope or severe symptoms may require urgent assessment. Reconcile tamoxifen and other QT-prolonging medicines. No source-defined QTc dose ladder is provided.

cases.name: Electrolyte risk: assess severity without invented blanket hold

findings.text: Correct electrolyte abnormalities relevant to QT risk and obtain clinical/ECG review. Decide whether initiation or continuation should be deferred according to severity, symptoms and the prescribed product. The NCCP and Irish SmPC do not provide a universal numeric electrolyte hold threshold or automatic tamoxifen dose reduction.
Stop tamoxifen immediately and arrange urgent assessment for suspected SJS / TEN.
Do not restart tamoxifen after tamoxifen-associated SJS / TEN.

Severe thrombocytopenia or leucocytopenia requires individual risk–benefit review and close supervision under the Irish Tamox SmPC. Assess the cause and clinical severity. No universal ANC/platelet number or automatic chemotherapy-style reduction is supplied.

Assess and manage hypercalcaemia, including symptoms, severity and bone disease. The Irish Tamox SmPC requires individual risk–benefit review and supervision; it gives no numerical tamoxifen dose ladder for calcium.

Tamoxifen may induce or exacerbate hereditary angioedema. Review suitability and the emergency plan; acute tongue/throat swelling or breathing difficulty needs emergency assessment. A history alone is not a universal source contraindication.

The Irish Tamox SmPC advises against combining hormone preparations, particularly oestrogens, because effects may oppose each other. Review the exact preparation and non-hormonal alternatives with the prescriber; do not automatically apply this statement to every locally administered menopausal treatment.

The Irish Tamox SmPC advises avoiding platelet-aggregation inhibitors because bleeding may occur during thrombocytopenia. Reconcile the antiplatelet indication, blood count and bleeding risk with oncology/pharmacy and the prescribing team. Do not stop essential antiplatelet therapy without an agreed plan.

Intolerable symptoms merit Consultant review even without a high toxicity grade. Discuss symptom support, adherence and a suitable alternative endocrine plan; NCCP does not provide a universal percentage dose reduction.

Review lipid history and arrange lipid monitoring when clinically indicated: NCCP notes possible cholesterol/triglyceride increases in patients with pre-existing hyperlipidaemia. No automatic dose change is specified.

Intolerable symptoms merit Consultant review even without a high toxicity grade. Discuss symptom support, adherence and a suitable alternative endocrine plan; NCCP does not provide a universal percentage dose reduction.
